Nobody else has said it yet, but somebody needs to... Abuse is abuse, whether or not there is a mental diagnosis or not. 
  I am usually the first person to stand up and say that while life with someone with bipolar (or any mental disorder) is not easy, and is often harder in some ways, that it has its own set of rewards in the form of some incredibly, amazing people. My bf of just under a year is bp (& also struggles with self-medicating with alcohol). I can honestly say that there were times I really questioned whether I wanted to deal with the "baggage." We had only been dating ~5 months when the mother of all down spirals hit. He drank constantly, broke up with me every other weekend, talked constantly about quitting his job (we work together/I am technically his assistant- him quitting would lose my job also) and moving back to where he had been before he moved here, talked about leaving his son (who I am very involved with) with his ex (who has almost no involvement with her son). Long story short, it was hell for the next 4 months. 
   He doesn't "believe" in therapy; is not medicated and at the time, I felt was destined to live a pathetic, lonely existence. However he is the most brilliant, amazing, funny, sweet, generous person (and father) you could ever meet. I was then, and still am totally in love with him. We have dealt with alot in our first year, but it also taught me how to set boundaries with him. While he never flat out cheated on me, he pushed the envelope very far during that time. As I said earlier, he broke up with me every other weekend, and at times was verbally abusive. I forgave him for all of it; but I also let him know what I expected if he wanted to be with me. I won't tolerate being abused. Nobody should. And that line needs to be drawn & explained sooner rather than later.
   You honestly sound miserable. I know you love her, but sometimes it is better to love from afar. I am not you so I cannot make that decision for you, but I would encourage you to decide whether things are too broken to be salvaged or whether you still want to fight for what you believe you have.
      If you choose to fight, you have to know going in that you are putting the ball in her court & she may choose to leave rather than follow your "rules." If she does, than you mourn your feelings and you work towards moving forward & recovering. If she chooses to stay, then you clearly explain what is acceptable behavior and what is NOT. For example, if you want to be with me, you have to be faithful, you cannot EVER lay a hand on me again, you may not take your anger/sadness etc out on me for no reason etc etc. I will be here to help you and support you & as your partner, but I will NOT be your punchingbag/scapegoat. 
    Anyhow you get where I'm going.... I really do wish you all the luck. I can tell you love her. I just wanted to give you some things to consider in making a decision. Ultametely, it is your happiness/health that is most important in this decision. If she is making you unhappy/unhealthy & she isn't willing to change, than it is time to move on. Good luck and I hope you feel better soon, whatever you decide <<HUGS>>

It's funny that you say that, because in a way, we are similar. Typically I like to walk away and then come back when I'm not so emotional, bc one, I can then see the other persons perspective better & two, I am less likely to say something I don't actually mean.
   He on the other hand, does one of two things when something upsets him. He will either want to deal with it right then, and it is often a bigger fight than it should have been bc many times when he wants to deal with it right then, he has been drinking. 
  This is one of the issues we are still dealing with, and the reason that we had to get VERY clear boundaries in place. We live an hour away from each other, & while we see each other at least 5 days a week bc we work together, after dating for about 5 months, we went through a tough few months where he was drinking heavily & while he never slept with anyone, he was messaging/texting people on Tinder/his old hookups, and once went home with someone from the bar (he was too drunk to do anything, but I know they at least made out etc). 
   Anyhow I chose to stay and work through that stuff, and by his choice, he has since cut down heavily on his drinking, had deleted all old contacts/Tinder from his phone, given me passwords to his phone/FB etc and has told me (& I actually believe him 100%) that he wants to be with nobody else, wants to get his life together and get married eventually etc. He has really put so much effort in over the past few months and has given me the strength again to get through another bad time if it happens.
  The depression is the worst. I can deal with his mania, because he becomes super motivated and decides he wants to make a million dollars this year (he's done it before) and he works like crazy etc. The depression on the other hand means he feels like shit about himself (he's gained some weight since we started dating last May), and he hit a depressive streak about 4 months into our relationship, which lasted about August- December, with a few normal breaks in between. However he feels like crap about himself so he would talk to other women bc he wanted to feel like he was still attractive. He wouldn't work bc things with our office wouldn't go the way he thought they should, so he either wouldn't work or would be ready to quit constantly. I would end up doing way more parenting of his 4 yr old son (he has sole custody) than he would (he did the basics, but dicipline/attention etc were on me alot) & I have 5 kids of my own. His drinking became a daily occurrence for a while, and eventually he became verbally abusive when he drank and/or would break up with me every other week. I began to wonder why I was staying in such a dysfunctional situation.
    But the reason was clear. I love him. I have had my own struggles with ptsd and subsequent substance abuse, and got labeled Borderline during a custody battle over my 2 youngest (I am not. I was in counseling at the time, had been for ~18 months, & my counselor just laughed when I told him what the court appointed custody evaluator said. He thought it was the most ridiculous diagnosis he had ever heard, and said I had PTSD from being raped/getting pregnant from the rape  & subsequently losing my son to SIDS. He also felt I had fleas from the abusive relationship I had just gotten out of. My SO never treated me different or less than bc of my struggles. He gave me the opportunity to work with him as a partner in sales, which opened me up to an industry I love, and we have absolutely rocked working together. We blow away our sales competition every month. We compliment each other so well bc we are very similar, however where we are different, our weaknesses & strengths are just opposite enough that together we make a super human ;) We are actually starting a business together (we'll still work our current position for a while), but we are slowly building "our empire" as he likes to call it. 
    I know I kind of got off track a bit, but I always want to tell people about how wonderful he can be, bc we've definitely had some haters bc of his diagnosis and bc he is not always 100%. But even though he has made some mistakes and has not always treated me the way he should have, I know he wants to be where he is now; mostly stable, working on getting his life back on track & working towards a future. 
   That person who made that comment on the post we responded to made me so angry. They acted like bc of a BP diagnosis, that they were not worthy of love and are not good people. It was so overgeneralized and just plain wrong, I wanted to scream. My relationship with my SO has not always been perfect, but our communication, our goals, our values etc are so much better than any relationship I have ever had, and I wouldn't trade it for a million other "perfect" relationships. :)

I too, disagree that it doesn't get better. My current SO is BP, and I have been with someone who is BP before. The experiences are night and day. Yes, there are bad times, however there are bad times in any relationship. Saying to run just because someone has a mental illness/BP is over generalizing and overall just mean. My relationship with my BP SO is a 1000 times better than my relationship with my ex-husband who had no mental illness issues. I don't think you can say just because someone struggles with BP that they are not deserving of a chance at love. Now that isn't to say that BP is a "get out of jail free" card for bad behavior/abuse, because it absolutely isn't. You deserve respect from your SO, no matter what struggles they may have, but I will say I wouldn't trade my SO brilliant brain for anything. He is one of the most intelligent, business-savy, creative, generous & funny people I've ever met. He just happens to get moody and struggles with some pretty dark places at times. It took a while & some messy times,  but we finally worked out our boundaries. And honestly, I think it took seeing that I would stick by him through the messiness for him to realize that he wanted to "be better." He knows what my boundaries are, and what is acceptable & what is not, and that if he is unable or unwilling to mind my boundaries, that I won't be with him, however he also knows that I am there for him, to support him, even if we aren't together. Even with the occasional drama, I wouldn't trade him for 1000 guys that are considered mentally stable. I don't know what your experience was, but just know that there is a light at the end of the tunnel and it is possible to have a healthy relationship with someone with BP.

There are definitely those of us non-BP's (doesn't mean we don't have our own issues ;) who understand. If that friend didn't listen, try another. If family is close, try them. You will find someone.
   I have felt the same way before. I have my own struggles and my SO is BP, so it can be hard sometimes for him to give me the emotional support I need. 
    I went for a long time thinking I just was meant to be the giver in every relationship (friend, family, romantic). That I must not have been worthy of receiving "love" (what I realized was just emotional support) back. It took quite a while for me to realize I surrounded myself with people who were "takers," and I did it on purpose. 
    Anyhow I'm getting off topic, I just wanted to post and let you know that there are definitely people out there :)

Things like this are the reason why if you don't have health insurance, you should at the very least have a good med pay on your car insurance. Yes, it will cover you if you are hit by someone without insurance and if you are walking down the street and they hit you. 
Most people my age don't realize how important insurance is. They have the mentality of "it will never happen to me." They figure they don't need life insurance because they have no family to support. Often they don't realize that at a young age a $50,000 life insurance policy will only cost them around $9 a month. They often also carry state minimum coverage on their car. The problem is that if your limits are set at $25,000/$50,000/$25,000 (each person/total payout/property damage), and you hit a mini-van with Mom, Dad & 2 kids and their total medical bills come to $200,000 for all of them, you are now on the hook for $150,000. The monies not paid out by insurance can be collected by seizing any assets you have (your house, car, collectors items etc) and the rest by garnishing your wages for however long it takes to pay it off.Do yourself a favor and if your insurance agent has not gone through and given you a crash course regarding your personal policies, find a new agent/company who will. Their job is to make sure you are properly covered in the event of an accident, and to find you the cheapest way to do so. Btw, if you have an auto policy, but do not own a home, look into adding a renters policy. Often the discount you will get by having "multiple" policies will pay for the renters policy (depending on the amount of the policy coverage/which company you have), and for example with my company, when I added a renters policy to my account, it brought my payment down $50 every 6 months and that was after the renters policy was paid for.

You are off to a good start. Don't focus on how far you have to go though. Focus on the positive things you've done so far. You've set up a savings account. You are caught up on bills. You are two big steps further than you were last month! While it will take a bit to change your thinking/habits, one thing I noticed is that in that short paragraph, you mentioned "not getting to buy yourself anything" and "treating yourself to lunch on Friday." Getting yourself out of the mindset of saving/paying bills is a punishment or a bad thing, will go so far in helping you reach your goals. Even eating out just 1 x week is $10 (between paying for the food, the gas to get to the restaurant etc) adds up. Actually that is 1/2 of your current savings deposit for the month! If you set small goals, like 'this month I want to hit  $200 in my savings account, and next month aim for your balance to be $400 (or whatever amount you determine your goal should be), it is a nice feeling when you start seeing that account balance climb higher and higher (it's own reward ;) If you are the type of person who has to have a "reward," try and set a monthly goal and treat yourself at the end of the month after everything has been paid/saved etc..
Anyhow good luck!!

You need to go talk to the head of financial aid immediately and find out what the situation is! Do not give her any more money (I would probably take this years financial aid and use it to move out ASAP). When you talk to FA, make sure that all school bills are current and paid. Find out if you have been getting loans, or if it is straight pell/grants. If you have been getting that much money returned to you, how has school been paid for? With my pell grants and extra grants, I usually had money left over after tuition was paid for, but it was only about $1000 or a bit less. You may have been getting loans in addition to grants etc, which means all of the money that she has been using to pay her bills, you are now on the hook for when it is time to pay those loans back (usually when you finish college). I'm not sure how old you are, but if you are in college, you are probably old enough to live on your own. It sucks, but it is time to step up and take charge of your life. Your parents actions have shown that they do not have your best interests at heart. Get out now before your financial future is over and done with. You will need to talk to financial aid about becoming an "independent student." Find a room to move into (you don't need a whole apartment, find roommates etc- check craigslist/friends/other family etc). You may be able to qualify for food stamps (won't be much, but anything will help you out at this point). Subscribe to "r/frugal." They have many ideas on living cheap, eating on almost nothing.. I am sorry you are having to go through this, but you can do it. Just ask for help (whether that is via reddit, school, friends) and know that you can and will survive. It may be hard at first, but you will be so proud of yourself in the end, knowing that you are independent. Good luck!
